## Setup

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(simling)
```

## The data

In `agreement_attraction`, 40 participants read sentences like *The key to the cabinet(s) was/were rusty* while an eye tracker records their eye movements. The verb is either grammatical (*was*) or ungrammatical (*were*), and the noun before it, the [attractor]{.hl}, is singular (*cabinet*) or plural (*cabinets*). `gaze_duration` is the time in ms that readers look at the verb the first time they reach it. It is `NA` when they skipped the verb.

```{r}
glimpse(agreement_attraction)
```

Today's question: does a plural attractor make an ungrammatical verb easier to read?

---

## 3. Weekly assignment

::: {.assignment .alert .alert-info}
Exercises 3.1 to 3.3 are this week's assignment. Complete them at home and hand in your .Rmd file within a week.
:::

In `acceptability`, 48 participants rate sentences on a scale from 1 (very bad) to 7 (very good). The sentences contain a long or a short dependency (`length`) between a *wh*-word and its gap, and the gap is inside an [island]{.hl} or not (`structure`). Islands are structures out of which a dependency is hard to form, such as *whether* clauses.

### 3.1 Cell means and plot

Compute the mean `rating` in each combination of `length` and `structure`, and make an interaction plot with `length` on the `x` axis and one line per `structure`. Are the lines parallel?


### 3.2 The model

```{r}

```

### 3.3 The island effect

An [island effect]{.hl} means that long dependencies out of islands are worse than the two effects on their own predict. Compute, from the cell means, how much ratings drop from short to long dependencies in non-islands, and how much in islands. Which coefficient of your model is the difference between the two drops? Is there an island effect?
